material_facts.description: Patient was involved in a 2-vehicle side-impact motor vehicle collision requiring mechanical extrication.
EMS and ED noted odor of alcohol and patient-reported drinking prior to driving, with elevated serum ethanol of 110 mg/dL confirmed at the hospital.
Patient sustained an open (compound) displaced mid-shaft left humerus fracture with active bleeding and 2.2cm overriding.
Patient sustained a displaced spiral fracture of the left distal radius with intra-articular extension and spiral deformity.
Patient had a 2cm superficial scalp laceration and mild altered mental status (GCS 14) at the scene.
Patient sustained a left knee contusion in the collision.
Acute cervical spine injury with C4-C7 tenderness, muscle spasm, and prevertebral soft tissue swelling consistent with trauma was diagnosed at the ED.
Left forearm/wrist showed weak radial pulse, delayed capillary refill, and decreased distal sensation at presentation, indicating neurovascular compromise.
Acute cervical spine imaging showed C5-C6 disc narrowing with a 6mm disc bulge and mild retrolisthesis, with onset noted as inconclusive by the radiologist.
One year prior to the MVA, patient had a cervical strain from heavy squat lifting with imaging showing a 4mm C5-C6 disc bulge and mild degenerative disc disease, without fracture.

On 2023-09-07, patient underwent left upper extremity reconstruction with ORIF via dynamic plate fixation of the humerus, volar plate fixation of the distal radius, and repair of the extensor tendon sheath.
Patient was hospitalized from 2023-09-04 to 2023-09-08 with IV antibiotics (Ancef/Cephalexin), IV/oral opioid pain management, ambulation with PT, and neuro checks before discharge.

Patient completed a 30-session outpatient physical therapy course (Sept-Dec 2023) with Robert Stewart, PT, DPT, addressing left upper extremity ROM/strength deficits and cervical spine pain, including several missed/no-show sessions.

Patient continued physical therapy with Amanda Gregory, PT, OCS from January to March 2024 addressing persistent muscle wasting, decreased ROM/strength, and chronic cervical disc bulge, until MMI was reached.
Patient missed multiple physical therapy appointments in November 2023 (no-shows on 11/14, 11/17, 11/21), with documented rebound in elbow stiffness before returning to treatment on 11/27/2023.
Following surgery, patient had persistent left radial nerve sensory deficit and wrist extension weakness documented through late 2023.
Follow-up cervical spine MRI in December 2023 showed progression of the C5-C6 disc bulge from 4mm (pre-accident) to 6mm with new left neural foraminal stenosis.
By December 2023 and confirmed February 2024, X-rays showed the left humerus and distal radius fractures were well-healed with stable hardware and complete bony fusion.
Treating surgeon opined that the motor vehicle accident exacerbated the patient's pre-existing cervical disc disease.

On 2024-03-14, the treating surgeon determined the patient reached Maximum Medical Improvement for the left upper extremity with permanent functional impairment, including 15-degree elbow flexion/extension deficit, 20-degree wrist supination deficit, permanently blunted radial hand sensation, and chronic mild-to-moderate neck pain.
Physical therapy discharge in March 2024 similarly documented MMI with a persistent 15-degree elbow extension deficit, sensory blunting over the radial hand, and chronic neck pain baseline of 3/10.
Patient was given a permanent work restriction of no lifting greater than 20 lbs with the left arm.
Patient was kept off full-duty work per surgeon's restrictions during the recovery period.
In April 2024, the surgeon recommended ongoing chronic pain management or surgical decompression for the cervical spine.
